details:
The primary reason that I subscribed to VRC+ was because EmmVRC and Remod allowed for additional features to be used with the VRC+ subscription -- primarily extra avatar storage slots. Not only were these mods not hurting the game, they actively encouraged users to subscribe to get more out of it and support the developers. I was happy to! My wife was too (she is also cancelling VRC+).
There were a number of critical features bundled into these mods and others in the Melon Loader list, and I will not be resubscribing to VRC+ until they are incorporated into the base game:
1: Avatar searching. I'm sorry. It's not just critical from a QOL and convenience perspective, it's critical for actual gameplay. The avatar is our single biggest choice on how we're presenting ourselves to the world, and for those of us like me who enjoy non-standard / non-humanoid avatars, finding ones I like is a beast of a job even WITH avatar searching. Without it? Fat chance. Not happening. So, I'm not having a great time, and I'm not as interested in playing. Beyond that, just looking for avatars IS part of the fun! When I'm chilling with my friends, we spend entire nights just chit-chatting while searching through and trying on avatars. It's a passive thing we can do to have fun while talking, hanging out and showing off cool avatars we're finding, sharing them, etc. Killing that kills a major source of fun for us in addition to making it more frustrating to find the basic things we need for personalizing our experiences.
2) Flight / Noclip: For anybody who enjoys using non-humanoid or avatars that are smaller than usual, flight / noclip is critical for interacting with the world and with our friends. It just is. It's also fun for exploration and sight seeing in larger worlds. World-owners can already limit this in the settings of their world, meaning it doesn't break any actual gameplay in games or competitive worlds, and adds a lot of functionality and enjoyment for social and artistic spaces. Killing this helps nothing and hurts plenty. Make it official.
3) Advanced safety settings, avatar draw distance, performance optimization: How is it that mods are providing better safety, security, and performance optimization settings than the base game, and your choice is to *get rid of them?* Performance and optimization mods are the only reason my wife's laptop can handle many VRC worlds at all, especially if there's more than a few people in them. Why? What possible benefit is there to you...?
Frankly, there are dozens of other incredible mods that improve the user interface, add new features, make appreciated quality of life improvements, etc. Even simple ones like spawning personal mirrors; viewing avatar hitboxes to make it easier to select a tiny or nonstandard avatar for cloning, adding friends, muting, or blocking people; etc.
While the top three are most important to me and to my wife, there are many others worth mentioning that are very important to many other people. You say that "many of these features" (without specifying which ones) have "been on our roadmap for years," as if that's some kind of comfort, but that's the entire problem. YEARS. Years for basic functionality to search content, to better navigate the world space, to configure graphics, camera, and optimization settings to individual needs... You say you're a small team and that this stuff takes time, but independent modders working for free managed just fine. Frankly, given that you already know these features WORK, you don't even HAVE to develop them. Just work with the modders to incorporate the functionality in the base game. Hire them, reward them, or even just offer to immortalize their work -- they're already doing this for free simply because they love VRChat-- and then improve upon it over time. You could have the core features people are begging for officially incorporated into the update in a matter of hours. The code is already written, playtested by thousands of users for months or years, and is universally enjoyed by those who benefit from them.
It's all just very frustrating. Mods make game better, and VRC in particular feels like an especially odd choice to crack down on mods for given that it's almost entirely non-competitive / strictly social. Rather than gutting the community's favorite resources for making your game even better, you should be working WITH the people who make those resources to improve compatibility and functionality with the base game!
Augh. My wife and I just bought computers specifically so we could play VRC, both happily subscribed, and now we're both frustrated and angry that the features that make the experience convenient, comfortable, possible, and fun are about to vanish overnight. We've already had to go through and erase our favorite avatar lists, try to condense to just <25 in preparation of cancelling VRC+. We may just be two people, but that's $20 a month you're not getting any more because you refused to listen to your community, and I know we're not alone in cancelling our subscriptions over this. 
Get it together, guys. Either incorporate support for these mods, or directly add their functionality to the core game BEFORE killing the mods that grant it. Work with the modders to make this happen. They've already figured it out -- you don't have to reinvent the wheel.
title: Cancelling VRC+ in light of killing mods. Critical features that must be incorporated before I'll resubscribe:
